Schwabing-West — Munich, Germany

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Schwabing-West is one of Munich's 25 official Stadtbezirke (city districts). Polizeipraesidium Muenchen and the Statistisches Amt Muenchen recorded 1,859 total offences here in 2025, across a population of 68,610 residents (31 December 2024) — a rate of 2,710 offences per 100,000 residents, roughly 0.5x the citywide average, below it. This rate is calculated against registered residents, not footfall, so a busy central, station, or nightlife-heavy district can read higher without that meaning it is unusually risky to walk through, and a quiet residential district can show a low rate simply by having few offences relative to its population. This is Wandroz's official-data layer for Munich — real Polizeipraesidium Muenchen / Statistisches Amt Muenchen figures, not a qualitative or press-based judgment — and the source data is not split here by time of day, so both figures shown here are the same.

Frequently asked questions

Is Schwabing-West safe?

Wandroz currently rates Schwabing-West in Munich, Germany as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Schwabing-West safe at night?

At night, Schwabing-West is rated as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.
